Case 1: 5x + 7 ≤ 0

x ≤ -&frac{7}{5}

Case 2: 5x + 7 > 0
5x > -7
x > -&frac{7}{5}

Now, solve for each case:

For Case 1: |5x + 7| ≥ 12 becomes 5x + 7 ≥ 12
5x ≥ 5
x ≥ 1
Since x must also be less than or equal to -&frac{7}{5}, the solution for this case is x = 1 (only one value)

For Case 2: |5x + 7| ≥ 12 becomes -(5x + 7) ≥ 12
-5x - 7 ≥ 12
-5x ≥ 19
x ≤ -&frac{19}{5}
Since x must also be greater than -&frac{7}{5}, the solution for this case is -&frac{7}{5} < x ≤ -&frac{19}{5}
